title: UV lamps: how to track operating time and stay within service life
excerpt: A lamp lasts 8,000–9,000 hours: it still shines, but no longer disinfects. What to record, how to calculate operating time, and why it must never be switched on when people are present.

body.text: A UV germicidal lamp is an inexpensive, effective way to reduce airborne microbes in a production area and on surfaces. But a lamp does not last forever: each model has a service life, usually 8,000–9,000 hours. After that, it may still shine while its germicidal effectiveness is gone.

items: Lamp replacement, including its part number and date.

body.title: Safety
body.text: An exposed germicidal lamp may operate only when no one is in the room. Switching it on between shifts while people are present can injure eyes and skin. Install a timer relay with a door interlock.

In an electronic log, the lamp has a counter: switching it on starts the timer, and switching it off stops it. As the lamp approaches the end of its service life, a replacement task is created automatically. No more guessing that the lamp is probably still good.
